title: Happy the Man to Whom His God
description: Happy the Man to Whom His God in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 32, part 2, headed “Free pardon and sincere obedience; or, Confession and forgiveness”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Hap-py the man to whom his God No more im-putes his sin, But wash'd in the Re-deem-er's blood, Hath made his gar-ments clean!

lines: Happy the man to whom his God
But wash'd in the Redeemer's blood,
And from the guilty bondage free,
His spirit hates deceit and lies,
He guards his heart, he guards his eyes,
While I my inward guilt supprest,
Thy wrath lay burning in my breast,
Then I confess'd my troubled thoughts,
Thy pardoning grace forgave my faults,
This shall invite thy saints to pray,
Temptations rise, our strength and stay

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
